requirements.text: Cheryl Osborne called us ... unable to connect to the internet ... raise a critical priority incident. Kindly log that
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_049' AND channel = 'phone' AND status = 'new' AND priority = 'critical' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100)
caller resolved from the seed: Cheryl Osborne is USER_049 (cheryl.osborne@servicenow.com, active, manager role, ORG_001), the only user with that name; the request treats her as the affected user
channel phone because she 'called us'; the policy's chat default applies only when no channel is given
status new is the policy's default state for a new incident (the column is status in this schema)
priority critical is stated; impact high and urgency high are the only pair in the policy's Impact x Urgency matrix that gives critical
short_description is mandatory but free text; category and org_id are not fixed by the request or policy; none is tested

requirements.text: raise a critical priority incident (policy: every incident created should have an SLA tagged based on priority)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_001' AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: implied by the policy (section 6), not stated in the request
SLA_001 is the seed's active response SLA with applies_to_priority = critical ('Priority 1 - Response', ORG_001)
stage in_progress kept from the benchmark check; the policy says the SLA starts when the priority is tagged
two SLA rows are created in this table, so the row is selected by its natural key (incident, definition), not by id

assumptions: implied by the policy (section 6), not stated in the request
SLA_002 is the seed's active resolution SLA with applies_to_priority = critical ('Priority 1 - Resolution', ORG_001); the policy tracks both response and resolution metrics
stage in_progress kept from the benchmark check; the policy says the SLA starts when the priority is tagged
two SLA rows are created in this table, so the row is selected by its natural key (incident, definition), not by id

requirements.text: SLA tagged based on priority (boundary: no SLA for another priority)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND sla_def_id NOT IN ('SLA_001', 'SLA_002')
assumptions: boundary of 'based on priority': the seed's six other definitions apply to high, moderate and low priority, and a loose 'link the SLAs' would sweep them in

requirements.text: provide a relevant knowledge article to be used as resolution to the issue
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_017' AND incident_kb_id = 'IKB_046' AND used_as = 'suggested'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_046 after IKB_045); the request asks for one article, so one link
KB_017 'Guest WiFi Access' (published, external) is the seed's only article on guest internet access (she 'tried connecting as a guest')

used_as suggested kept from the benchmark check: policy section 7 links articles found at incident creation as suggested and reserves resolution for an article that resolves the incident, which stays new here; 'to be used as resolution' is read as the article's purpose

disagreement: used_as: A suggested, B resolution; chose suggested because the benchmark's check is the prior and the request's phrase does not plainly contradict it: the incident is logged, not resolved, and policy 7 ties the resolution type to resolving the incident

requirements.text: provide a relevant knowledge article (boundary: not the near-match article)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_018'
assumptions: KB_018 'Slow Internet in Building B' is the only other article a loose search for 'internet' returns; it is a known-issue note about speed, not a resolution for a failure to connect, and the request asks for one article

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_031' AND incident_id = 'INC_101' AND email = 'cheryl.osborne@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_031 after NOTIF_030); the only notification the task creates, so anchored by id
email is the caller's seed email (USER_049), added because the request names the caller as the recipient
type update kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the policy's default 'other' applies only when no type is given)

Verify SLA.evidence: two incident_sla rows are created and the request fixes no order, so TSLA_027 and TSLA_028 cannot be bound to SLA_001 and SLA_002 by sequence position; carried as two requirements selected by (incident_id, sla_def_id) with the same stage and definitions, expected 1 each. The original's AND/OR precedence also lets its second branch match without incident_id = 'INC_101'.

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement (the incident INC_101, the two SLA rows selected by natural key, the KB_017 link at IKB_046, the notification NOTIF_031, and the two boundary stays) and on three of the four dispositions; the one contested cell is used_as on the knowledge link.
disagreement: value: used_as on the KB_017 link: A suggested (benchmark check kept), B resolution (benchmark check repaired from the request's words 'to be used as resolution'); chose suggested because the benchmark's check is the prior, policy section 7 links creation-time search results as suggested and reserves resolution for an article that resolves the incident, and the incident is logged as new, not resolved. A reviewer who reads the request's phrase as the link type rather than the article's purpose changes that one cell and sets 'Verify KB Tag' to repaired.
disagreement: disposition: 'Verify KB Tag': A kept, B repaired; kept, following the used_as decision above (same root, not a separate judgement).
disagreement: form: the two stay requirements and the SLA assumptions differ in wording only between the passes, with identical sql, expected and seed_count; kept A's wording with B's seed details folded in.
No assignment, category or short_description value is fixed by the request or policy, so none is tested. The caller holds the manager role on the seed; the request treats her as the affected user, so she is caller_id.
